idiom_name: typed conversion functions between the domain type and a declared message interface
implementation_notes: The message is a declared interface (ideally generated from the contract) and the mapper is a module of typed pure functions - toMessage(order: Order): OrderMessage and fromMessage(m: OrderMessage): Order - plus a discriminated union with switch once several message versions share a channel; the compiler then checks the mapping field by field, so an added field on either side fails at the mapper and nowhere else. Interfaces are erased at runtime, so the payload is unchecked: at a topic carrying foreign data a schema library validates before the mapper runs, and the mapper module imports both shapes while neither shape imports it.
pitfalls: A message interface is a compile-time fiction: JSON.parse(body) as OrderMessage bypasses the mapper, so decode through the mapper or a validator instead of casting.
strictNullChecks/exactOptionalPropertyTypes decide whether an absent wire field is visible to the compiler; without them the mapper quietly accepts undefined for required fields.
Numbers are doubles: ids above 2^53 and money must be carried as string or bigint and converted explicitly in the mapper.
Structural typing lets a message interface silently match a domain type with the same shape, hiding the boundary; name and document the contract type distinctly.

variants.name: zod schema with .transform as the inbound mapper
variants.idiom_name: z.object({...}).transform(...) validates and maps in one declaration
variants.implementation_notes: Declare the inbound message as a zod schema whose .transform produces the domain value, so validation, renaming and conversion are one declaration: z.object({ customer_id: z.string(), total_minor: z.number().int().nonnegative() }).transform(m => Order.rehydrate(...)) with safeParse deciding whether a bad payload raises or is routed to the invalid-message channel. Use it where producers are untrusted or the contract is only documented; the outbound direction usually stays a typed function because the domain side is trusted.
pitfalls: The transform's output type is the domain value, so the schema no longer describes the wire message: keep a raw schema (or z.input) when the payload shape still matters.
parse throws by default, and a throw inside a consumer usually means redelivery: choose safeParse plus an invalid-message route, or fail fast by policy.
Schemas assembled per consumer duplicate the contract; keep one schema per message type and share it, or the versions drift.
